classification: Source-informed virtual engineering probes; not independent fifty-case forecasts or empirical chemical accuracy.
setup_witnesses: Setup and one-dose titration complete without parser/numeric/solver refusal or silent fallback; archive actual capabilities and solver identity.
At end of setup, total NH3 across the screened vessel contents is at or below 1e-12 mol.
For the positive probe, a reviewed hypochlorite key NaOCl/ClO-/HClO remains above 1e-12 mol before and after the accepted dose.
final_witnesses: After the accepted dose, NH3 in the screened vessel exceeds 1e-12 mol.
Exactly one Titrated event records one accepted full dose: 0.000001 mol NaOH for 0.001 L at 0.001 mol/L; target pH12 is a stopping bound, not an expected chemistry value.
positive_expected: On pre-repair source, qualifying newly introduced exposure lacks the final chloramine warning. Preserve that baseline before judging the repair.
On repaired source, exactly one Danger bleach-ammonia-chloramine HazardWarning appears in the titration step with existing reviewed hazard/real_world metadata.
No chloramine warning is attributed to setup when the independently declared setup witnesses hold.
negative_expected: Benign counterpart has no hypochlorite key and no chloramine HazardWarning in the titration step; still record the accepted dose and actual final NH3 witness.
non_exercising_disposition: If any declared setup/final witness is absent, classify this protocol as not exercising the intended final-novelty route. Preserve raw outputs; do not count it as repair proof, adjust thresholds to outputs, or replace expectations silently. Diagnose author assumptions, backend coverage, trace reconstruction or solver failure separately.
scope: Two unrun targeted CLI probes, separate from unchanged100-case replay. Synthetic native16-function controls establish routing only; these probes seek an actual standard-stack exposure. No supported-real-chemistry/phase/concentration coverage claim yet.
